lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Independent application A: indirect measurement of inaccessible lengths

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One reference example. Use it only if you get stuck.

items.prompt: A 2 m pole casts a 3 m shadow; a tree casts a 12 m shadow. Tree height?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Two triangles with all three pairs of sides in the same ratio are similar. Which statement correctly justifies it?
choices: This is the SSS congruence criterion applied directly.
The criterion holds only when the ratio is a whole number.
This is the SSS similarity criterion: a dilation matches one triangle’s sides to the other’s, and the resulting figures are congruent.
Equal ratios of sides guarantee congruence, not similarity.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF. Side AB = 7 corresponds to DE = 14. If BC = 7, find EF.
In a right triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse divides it into segments of length 4 and 4. Find the altitude.
A 5 m pole casts a 8 m shadow. At the same moment a building casts a 64 m shadow. How tall is the building?
A line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally. Which statement correctly justifies it?
choices: The parallel line bisects both sides by definition.
The result follows from the Pythagorean theorem applied twice.
The parallel line creates corresponding angles, giving a smaller triangle similar to the original by AA, so the sides are in proportion.
The two parts of each side are congruent because the line is parallel.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF. Side AB = 15 corresponds to DE = 60. If BC = 13, find EF.
In a right triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse divides it into segments of length 9 and 9. Find the altitude.
A 6 m pole casts a 2 m shadow. At the same moment a building casts a 14 m shadow. How tall is the building?
choices: 5 m

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: The Pythagorean theorem can be proved using similarity. Which statement correctly justifies it?
choices: Similarity gives a² + b² = c² only for isosceles right triangles.
The theorem follows from the triangle inequality.
The altitude to the hypotenuse creates two triangles similar to the original; writing both similarity proportions and adding them yields a² + b² = c².
The theorem follows because all right triangles are similar to each other.
